before.problem: A learner stops at $2(2x^2+2x-12)$ while factoring $4x^2+4x-24$. Complete the factorization.
before.solution_sketch: Extract the remaining $2$ to get $4(x^2+x-6)$. The constants $3,-2$ multiply to $-6$ and add to $1$.

after.problem: A learner stops at $2(x^2+x-6)$ while factoring $2x^2+2x-12$. Complete the factorization.
after.solution_sketch: The GCF $2$ has been extracted. In the remaining trinomial, $3$ and $-2$ multiply to $-6$ and add to $1$. Thus the complete factorization is $2(x-2)(x+3)$.

rationale: Retain the existing GCF2–3 scope and the intended GCF-first-then-trinomial progression. The previous example has greatest coefficient factor4, outside that scope. The replacement tests completing the remaining trinomial after the first stage, instead of introducing an out-of-range remaining numerical GCF.
